# _wn_build_stamp <dir> <pkg> -- print where the build stamp for a package lives:
# a file under the worktree's own git directory, so it is per-worktree and never
# appears in the work tree or in what git status reports. Outside a git work tree
# it prints nothing.
_wn_build_stamp() {
  local gitdir
  gitdir="$(git -C "$1" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  [ -n "$gitdir" ] || return 1
  printf '%s/provision-stamps/%s\n' "$gitdir" "$(printf '%s' "$2" | tr '/' '_')"

# _wn_input_fingerprint <dir> <pkg> [source...] -- print a fingerprint of the
# git-tracked inputs a build consumes: what is on disk under the package and under
# any extra source path the list names. An edit, deletion or rename counts whether
# or not it is staged, because every tracked path is described from the work tree
# rather than from the index, and time stamps play no part. Untracked build
# products do not count.
_wn_input_fingerprint() {
  local dir="$1" pkg="$2"
  shift 2
  local path target blob description="" hashed="" i=0
  local -a files=()
  # Paths in this repository contain no newlines, so a newline-separated
  # --stdin-paths list and one line per path in the description stay unambiguous.
  while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
    if [ -L "$dir/$path" ]; then
      target="$(readlink "$dir/$path")" || return 1
      description+="L $path $target"$'\n'
    elif [ -f "$dir/$path" ]; then
      files+=("$path")
    else
      description+="D $path"$'\n'
    fi
  done < <(git -C "$dir" ls-files -z -- "$pkg" "$@")

  if [ "${#files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    hashed="$(printf '%s\n' "${files[@]}" | git -C "$dir" hash-object --stdin-paths)" || return 1
    while IFS= read -r blob; do
      description+="F ${files[$i]} $blob"$'\n'
      i=$((i + 1))
    done <<< "$hashed"
  fi

  # Sorted by the path in the second field, so the description is stable.
  printf '%s' "$description" | LC_ALL=C sort -k2 | git -C "$dir" hash-object --stdin
}

# _wn_output_stale <dir> <pkg> <artifact> [source...] -- succeed and print why a
# built output must be rebuilt. Each successful build records a stamp holding the
# fingerprint of the tracked inputs it consumed, so a missing stamp means the
# output has no record of what produced it (unrecorded). A stamp whose fingerprint
# no longer matches what is on disk means the sources moved since that build
# (changed); edits, deletions and renames count whether or not they are staged.
# Time stamps are deliberately not compared: a source with a future modification
# time would then read as newer than every stamp and rebuild forever. Comparing
# against the stamp instead of the output also survives a build that emits nothing
# when its inputs are unchanged, which previously left an old output looking stale
# on every later provision. Untracked files a build writes, such as nested dist
# folders and tsbuildinfo, never count. Outside a git work tree nothing is stale.
_wn_output_stale() {
  local root="$1" pkg="$2" stamp current
  shift 3

  stamp="$(_wn_build_stamp "$root" "$pkg")" || return 1
  if [ ! -f "$stamp" ]; then
    echo unrecorded
    return 0
  fi
  current="$(_wn_input_fingerprint "$root" "$pkg" "$@")" || return 1
  if [ "$current" = "$(cat "$stamp")" ]; then
    return 1
  fi
  echo changed
}

worktree-naming.sh <command> [args]

  allocate  [worktrees|branches]    Reserve the next number (locked; writes high-water).
  next      [worktrees|branches]    Preview the next number (no lock/write).
  scan-max  [worktrees|branches]    Highest number currently in use in a namespace.

  validate-pair   <branch> <dir>
  validate-backup <branch>          Exit 0 when the branch is a backup/* safety ref.
  validate-remote-allowlist <branch>  Check the remote-push-permission allowlist.
  create          <slug> [base] [--no-provision]  Returns 3 when the worktree was created but provisioning failed.
                                    Create a worktrees/NNN-slug worktree and install its deps.
  provision       [dir]             Install the dependency trees a worktree needs and build the outputs the list names (idempotent).
  create-branch   <slug> [base]     Create a branches/NNN-slug branch (no worktree).
  create-detached <slug> [base]     Create a numbered detached worktree.
USAGE
}

content.text:
local dir="${1:-}" list pkg artifact sources installed=0 built=0 skipped=0 failed=0
  local tool deps_root install_log build_reason stale_reason top built_fingerprint
  local -a install_cmd build_cmd
  # Allocation scans the shared clone, but provisioning must use the current worktree.
  [ -n "$dir" ] || dir="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || { echo "not in a git repo" >&2; return 1; }
  [ -d "$dir" ] || { echo "no such worktree: $dir" >&2; return 1; }
  # The dependency walk stops where it meets this path, so it must be absolute
  # and resolved like the paths the walk compares it with.
  dir="$(cd "$dir" && pwd -P)" || { echo "cannot resolve worktree: $dir" >&2; return 1; }
  # The list holds paths relative to the worktree root, so a subdirectory means that root.
  if top="$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" && [ -n "$top" ]; then
    dir="$(cd "$top" && pwd -P)" || { echo "cannot resolve worktree: $top" >&2; return 1; }
  fi
  list="$(_wn_provision_paths_file)" || return 1
  [ -f "$list" ] || { echo "missing provision path list: $list" >&2; return 1; }

  while read -r pkg artifact sources; do
    case "$pkg" in ''|\#*) continue ;; esac
    # A listed path that lost its manifest is a stale list entry, so name it.
    if [ ! -f "$dir/$pkg/package.json" ]; then
      echo "  WARNING: $pkg is listed but has no package.json; skipped" >&2
      continue
    fi
    # A bun lockfile, text bun.lock or binary bun.lockb, with no npm lockfile marks
    # a bun package. That lockfile pins versions an ancestor's npm tree need not
    # match, so only the package's own node_modules counts, and an npm install
    # there would write a second lockfile.
    if { [ -f "$dir/$pkg/bun.lock" ] || [ -f "$dir/$pkg/bun.lockb" ]; } \
      && [ ! -f "$dir/$pkg/package-lock.json" ]; then
      tool=bun; deps_root="$dir/$pkg"
    else
      tool=npm; deps_root="$dir"
    fi

    if _wn_deps_satisfied "$dir/$pkg" "$deps_root"; then
      skipped=$((skipped + 1))
    else
      _wn_have_tool "$tool" "$pkg" || { failed=$((failed + 1)); continue; }
      # npm ci needs a lockfile and a failed install cannot be followed by a build.
      # The installer's output goes to a log, not the terminal, so no --silent:
      # npm's silent level would drop the error lines a failure needs.
      if [ "$tool" = bun ]; then
        install_cmd=(bun install --frozen-lockfile)
      elif [ -f "$dir/$pkg/package-lock.json" ]; then
        install_cmd=(npm ci --no-audit --no-fund)
      else
        install_cmd=(npm install --no-audit --no-fund)
      fi
      echo "  provisioning $pkg (${install_cmd[0]} ${install_cmd[1]})" >&2
      install_log="$(mktemp)"
      if ( cd "$dir/$pkg" && "${install_cmd[@]}" >"$install_log" 2>&1 ); then
        installed=$((installed + 1))
        rm -f "$install_log"
      else
        echo "  FAILED: $pkg" >&2
        # A log with no error line must not end a caller running under set -e.
        grep -i -m 4 'error' "$install_log" | sed 's/^/    /' >&2 || true
        # A frozen install refuses a lockfile that no longer matches package.json.
        # Provisioning reports it rather than rewriting a committed lockfile unseen.
        if grep -qiE 'in sync|lockfile had changes' "$install_log"; then
          echo "    lockfile drift: package.json and its lockfile disagree; run ${install_cmd[0]} install in $pkg and commit the lockfile" >&2
        fi
        rm -f "$install_log"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
        continue
      fi
    fi

    build_reason=""
    if [ -n "$artifact" ]; then
      if [ ! -e "$dir/$pkg/$artifact" ]; then
        build_reason=missing
      # The list's paths contain no spaces, so the unquoted split into arguments is safe.
      elif stale_reason="$(_wn_output_stale "$dir" "$pkg" "$artifact" $sources)"; then
        build_reason=stale
      fi
    fi
    if [ -n "$build_reason" ]; then
      _wn_have_tool "$tool" "$pkg" || { failed=$((failed + 1)); continue; }
      # bun passes flags after the script name on to the script, so its flag goes first.
      if [ "$tool" = bun ]; then build_cmd=(bun run --silent build); else build_cmd=(npm run build --silent); fi
      if [ "$build_reason" = stale ]; then
        if [ "$stale_reason" = unrecorded ]; then
          echo "  rebuilding $pkg (no record of the sources it was built from)" >&2
        else
          echo "  rebuilding $pkg (sources changed since its last build)" >&2
        fi
      else
        echo "  building $pkg" >&2
      fi
      # Fingerprint the inputs before the build, not after: a build that edits its
      # own sources must leave that edit visible to the next provision.
      built_fingerprint="$(_wn_input_fingerprint "$dir" "$pkg" $sources)" || built_fingerprint=""
      if ! ( cd "$dir/$pkg" && "${build_cmd[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 ); then
        echo "  FAILED: $pkg build" >&2
        failed=$((failed + 1))
      elif [ ! -e "$dir/$pkg/$artifact" ]; then
        echo "  FAILED: $pkg build left $artifact missing" >&2
        failed=$((failed + 1))
      else
        # A stamp that cannot be written only costs a rebuild next time, so it never
        # fails provisioning, which callers run under set -e. With no fingerprint
        # taken before the build there is nothing trustworthy to record.
        if [ -n "$built_fingerprint" ]; then
          _wn_record_build "$dir" "$pkg" "$built_fingerprint" || :
        fi
        built=$((built + 1))
      fi
    fi
  done < "$list"

  echo "provisioned: $installed installed, $built built, $skipped already present, $failed failed" >&2
  [ "$failed" -eq 0 ]
}

--- title: "Implementation Plan: Phase 8: playbook-run-in-worktree" description: "Create one disposable sk-git worktree from the operator's BASE_REF, provision it with its own dependencies and build, run the eight phase 007 scenarios from their own command blocks, and publish a report package with one verdict per scenario." trigger_phrases: - "playbook run in worktree plan" - "disposable worktree scenario runner" - "manual testing playbook report package" importance_tier: "normal" contextType: "general" --- # Implementation Plan: Phase 8: playbook-run-in-worktree --- ## 1. SUMMARY ### Technical Context | Aspect | Value | |--------|-------| | **Language/Stack** | Markdown, Bash, Node, npm, git, ripgrep, jq | | **Framework** | system-spec-kit validator and guards, sk-git worktree allocator | | **Storage** | TSV, JSON and text files under this phase's `scratch/`, plus one report folder | | **Testing** | Each scenario file is its own script, compared to a frozen pattern | ### Overview One conductor creates a disposable worktree from the operator's `BASE_REF`, lets the sk-git allocator install that worktree's own dependency trees and build, and proves the build resolves inside the worktree. The conductor then reads the eight scenario rows from the phase 007 playbook index, extracts each scenario's own command block, runs it from the worktree root, captures the output and compares it to a frozen pattern. A failing scenario gets one fix brief and one rerun, at most three times, then an escalation row. The runs are assembled into the benchmark report package before the worktree is removed. --- ## 2. QUALITY GATES ### Definition of Ready - [ ] The launch preconditions in `../spec.md` section 3 are recorded as met in `../goal.md` section 4 - [ ] `BASE_REF` is recorded in `../goal.md` section 4 and resolves with `git rev-parse --verify` - [ ] Phase 007 is closed: every new scenario file exists and the playbook index lists it - [ ] `tasks.md` T001 to T003 are done: preconditions, tools and start state recorded ### Definition of Done - [ ] Every row in `acceptance-criteria.md` is `Met`, `Waived` or `Superseded` - [ ] `bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh --strict` prints `RESULT: PASSED` - [ ] `results.csv` holds eight data rows and every row is `PASS` or an escalated `FAIL` - [ ] The disposable worktree is gone and the primary checkout gate prints nothing outside the allowed paths - [ ] The frontier review ran read-only and its reply is saved --- ## 3. ARCHITECTURE ### Pattern One disposable execution host, one scenario map, one literal runner, one comparator, one report assembler. ### Key Components | Component | Role | |-----------|------| | **Conductor** | One DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session outside OpenCode. It creates the worktree, runs every command, writes every verdict and edits only this phase folder plus the report folder | | **Worktree allocator** | `.skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh create`, which allocates `worktrees/NNN-slug`, creates `.worktrees/NNN-slug` and provisions the dependency trees and builds | | **Scenario map builder** | A Node script that reads the playbook index, selects exactly one row per S label and writes `scratch/scenarios.tsv` | | **Runner** | A Bash script that extracts the `### Commands` fenced block from one scenario file and runs it from the worktree root | | **Comparator** | A Node script that matches each captured run against two frozen patterns and prints `PASS` or `FAIL` with a one-line reason | | **S8 worker** | One `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max` that authors a Level 1 packet from the card inside the disposable worktree | | **Fix worker** | One dispatch per failed attempt, limited to the one file the scenario's source table names | | **Reviewer** | One read-only `cli-codex` dispatch at phase close | ### 3.1 Execution host Two roots are named once by the conductor: - `RUNROOT`: the checkout that holds this phase folder and receives every durable write. It is the build worktree from `../goal.md` section 4 when the operator chose A, otherwise the primary checkout. - `MAIN`: the primary checkout, read with `git -C "$RUNROOT" worktree list --porcelain | awk 'NR==1{print $2}'`. `PHASE` is `$RUNROOT/specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/008-playbook-run-in-worktree`. `WT` is the absolute directory printed by the allocator. `WT_BRANCH` is the branch name printed beside it. `BASE_REF` is the ref the operator recorded in `../goal.md` section 4. The disposable worktree is created from `BASE_REF`, never from the conductor's uncommitted tree: ```bash bash .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh create playbook-run "$BASE_REF" \ > "$PHASE/scratch/worktree/create.out" 2> "$PHASE/scratch/worktree/create.err" read -r WT_BRANCH WT_DIR < "$PHASE/scratch/worktree/create.out" ``` The allocator prints ` ` on stdout and its provisioning lines on stderr. It exits 3 when the worktree exists but provisioning failed. In that case the conductor runs `bash .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh provision "$WT_DIR"` once. A second failure stops the phase with `BLOCKED provisioning`. ### 3.2 Own-code proof A fresh worktree holds no `node_modules` and no `dist`. A wholesale link of either would make the run read the primary checkout's code. The allocator installs each package inside the worktree instead. The conductor proves the result with this Node block, run from `$RUNROOT`, and writes its output to `scratch/worktree/own-code.txt`: ```bash node -e ' const fs = require("fs"); const path = require("path"); const skill = process.argv[1]; const root = fs.realpathSync(process.argv[2]) + path.sep; for (const t of ["runtime/dist", "node_modules", "node_modules/@spec-kit/runtime", "node_modules/@spec-kit/cli", "node_modules/@spec-kit/shared", "runtime/node_modules"]) { const p = path.join(skill, t); if (!fs.existsSync(p)) { console.log("MISSING " + t); continue; } const real = fs.realpathSync(p); console.log((real.startsWith(root) ? "OWN " : "FOREIGN ") + t); }' "$WT/.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit" "$WT" ``` A `FOREIGN` line is a hard stop. A `MISSING runtime/node_modules` line is allowed, as phase 003 records. The built orchestrator is `$WT/.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/dist/lib/validation/orchestrator.js`. ### 3.3 Scenario map (frozen selection rule) Phase 007 owns the scenario ids and file paths. This phase never guesses them. The map builder reads the playbook index and selects one row per S label with the title patterns below. The table also freezes the two pass patterns the comparator uses. | S | Subject | Index title pattern | Pass pattern A | Pass pattern B | |---|---------|---------------------|----------------|----------------| | S1 | Placeholder gate warns in Draft and strict passes | `placeholder.*Draft\|Draft.*placeholder` | `unfilled value token\(s\) in a Draft packet` | `RESULT: PASSED` | | S2 | Placeholder gate errors at Complete | `placeholder.*Complete\|placeholder.*error\|Complete.*placeholder` | `placeholder\(s\) found` | `RESULT: FAILED` | | S3 | A v2.2 doc keeps its old verdict | `placeholder.*v2\.2\|v2\.2.*placeholder\|legacy.*placeholder\|placeholder.*unchanged` | `placeholder\(s\) found` | `RESULT: FAILED` | | S4 | Example drift guard catches a leaked description | `example.*drift\|drift.*example` | `EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK` | empty | | S5 | Golden render holds for every level | `golden` | `Tests\s+12 passed \(12\)` | empty | | S6 | The router loads the card for four intents | `(router\|routing\|intent).*card\|card.*(router\|routing\|intent)` | `^4$` | `^0$` | | S7 | Card sync guard passes and fails on a broken copy | `card.*sync\|sync.*card` | `CARD SYNC OK` | empty | | S8 | DeepSeek authors a Level 1 packet from the card | `(DeepSeek\|weak model).*(author\|packet)\|(author\|packet).*(DeepSeek\|weak model)` | `RESULT: PASSED` | empty | A label with zero matches prints `MISSING S`. A label with two or more matches prints `AMBIGUOUS S`. Either one stops the map build. The conductor then records the blocker and stops, because a guessed scenario is worse than no run. The frozen patterns come from the code phases 003 to 005 ship: the warning text in `validatePlaceholders`, the PLACEHOLDER_FILLED message `placeholder(s) found`, the drift guard sentinel `EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK`, the golden test count `12 passed (12)`, the four intent count and the zero guide count, and the sync guard sentinel `CARD SYNC OK`. ### 3.4 Running one scenario The runner extracts the first fenced `bash` block under `### Commands`, writes it to `scratch/runs/.cmd` and runs it from `$WT`: ```bash awk ' /^### Commands[[:space:]]*$/ { section = 1; next } section && /^```bash[[:space:]]*$/ { block = 1; next } block && /^```[[:space:]]*$/ { exit } block { print } ' "$SCENARIO_FILE" > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$ID.cmd" ``` An empty command file is `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and is not run. The run output goes to `$PHASE/scratch/runs/$ID.txt`, followed by an `exit=` line. The command block is the scenario's own text. The runner never retypes a command. S8 is the one exception. Its commands dispatch a worker, so the conductor extracts the `### Prompt` block, writes a worker brief from the skeleton in this plan, dispatches it inside `$WT`, and then checks the packet the worker returns. S8's packet path is frozen to `specs/zz-playbook-s8/001-card-authoring-smoke` so the check needs no parsing judgment. ### 3.5 Comparator For each run the comparator reads the two patterns and prints one line: `S PASS ` or `S FAIL ` Both patterns must match. The `^4$` and `^0$` patterns are matched with the multiline flag. When a run does not match, the conductor reads the scenario's own `### Pass / Fail` section. If that section states a different observable and the run satisfies it, the row is `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and is escalated to phase 007. The comparator's verdict is never overridden by a chat impression. ### 3.6 Report package An existing report folder holds `README.md`, `results.csv`, `source.md` and `outcomes/`. This phase copies that real file set. The `sk-create-benchmark` report contract requires ten numbered sections, so `README.md` carries all ten section headings even though the older folders use a shorter shape. That difference is recorded in ADR-003. The report folder name is `--manual-testing-playbook--weak-model-authoring`, where the date is the run date from `date +%F`. When the folder exists, the conductor appends `-2`, `-3` and so on, because a report folder is immutable. `results.csv` uses the header observed in the existing folders: ```text scenario_id,runtime,run,evidence_class,verdict ``` One data row per scenario, with `runtime` set to `conductor`, `run` set to `1`, `evidence_class` set to `manual-testing-playbook` and `verdict` set to the row's verdict. `outcomes/.json` follows the observed shape: ```json { "scenarioId": "", "runtime": "conductor", "evidenceClass": "manual-testing-playbook", "verdict": "PASS", "reason": "", "executionContext": { "evidenceRoot": ".", "requireDurableEvidence": true }, "supersedes": [], "providerModel": null, "dispatchModel": "llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max", "runs": [ { "run": "1", "verdict": "PASS", "reason": "", "operatorInputs": "None.", "evidence": [ { "path": "specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/008-playbook-run-in-worktree/scratch/runs/.txt", "bytes": 0, "sha256": "" } ] } ], "evidence": [ { "path": "specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/008-playbook-run-in-worktree/scratch/runs/.txt", "bytes": 0, "sha256": "" } ] } ``` The `bytes` and `sha256` values are filled from `wc -c` and `shasum -a 256`. The example above is a shape, not a literal file. The conductor writes each file from the template in `tasks.md` T013. `source.md` names the scenario files, the run files, the worktree branch and path, `BASE_REF` and the phase folder. `README.md` ends with a file table and a REPRODUCIBILITY section that holds the create, provision and run commands. One row is added at the top of `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/README.md`: ```text | | [`/`](.//) | conductor manual-testing-playbook |

PASS, FAIL | **** | `manual-testing-playbook` | ``` ### 3.7 Failure protocol A `FAIL` row gets one fix brief and one rerun. The same scenario gets at most three fix briefs. After the third failed fix the row becomes `ESCALATED` and the other scenarios continue. The one file a fix may touch is the first row of the scenario file's `## 4. SOURCE FILES` table under `### Implementation And Test Anchors`. The conductor copies that path into the brief and into ALLOWED WRITE PATHS. No second file is allowed. The fix brief is the skeleton in the AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL section, followed by this text with the four fields filled: ```text TASK: Scenario failed at . The captured run is . The failing line is: The scenario's pass criterion is: Change only the single file named under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS so that the scenario passes. Do not edit the scenario file. Do not edit any other file. Run this command from the worktree root and paste its last line: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh --strict RETURN exactly one line: FIXED or BLOCKED ``` After the worker returns, the conductor reruns the same scenario command block from `$WT`. A PASS marks the row `FIXED` and keeps the original run beside the rerun as `scratch/runs/.fix-.txt`. ### Data Flow `BASE_REF`, then disposable worktree, then provable own-code build, then scenario map, then one captured run per scenario, then comparator verdict, then `results.tsv`, then report package, then worktree removal, then frontier review. --- ## FIX ADDENDUM: AFFECTED SURFACES This phase changes no product producer by hand. It reads the phase 007 scenarios and runs the phase 003 to 005 guards. A fix brief may change one file inside the disposable worktree, and that change is never merged by this phase. | Surface | Current Role | Action | Verification | |---------|--------------|--------|--------------| | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/manual-testing-playbook/` | Holds the eight new scenarios and the index | unchanged, read | `scratch/scenarios.tsv` names eight existing files | | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/check-example-drift.sh` | Example drift guard | unchanged, run by S4 | `EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK` in the S4 run | | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/check-card-sync.sh` | Card sync guard | unchanged, run by S7 | `CARD SYNC OK` in the S7 run | | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh` | Validation front end | unchanged, run by S1, S2, S3 and S8 | `RESULT:` line in each run | | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/README.md` | Report index | one row added | `rg -c` of the folder name prints `1` | Required inventories: - Same-class producers: the eight scenario files are the whole new set, selected by the eight S labels in `scratch/scenarios.tsv`. A missing label stops the run. - Consumers of changed symbols: the report index is the only consumer changed, and `rg -c` proves one row. - Matrix axes: eight scenarios by two pass patterns, 16 cells, each reported as a match or a miss. - Algorithm invariant: a scenario passes only when its captured run matches both frozen patterns. A disagreement with the scenario file is a scenario defect, never a silent pass. --- ## 4. IMPLEMENTATION PHASES Follow the ordered tasks in `tasks.md`. It owns the Setup, Implementation and Verification phase checkboxes and task state. --- ## 5. TESTING STRATEGY | Test Type | Scope | Tools | |-----------|-------|-------| | Unit | The extractor and comparator against a fixture scenario in `scratch/test/` | `run-scenario.sh`, `check-run.mjs` | | Integration | Each of the eight scenarios, on the disposable worktree | the scenario's own command block | | Manual | The frontier review reads every run and every verdict | read-only `cli-codex` dispatch in `tasks.md` T017 | --- ## 6. DEPENDENCIES | Dependency | Type | Status | Impact if Blocked | |------------|------|--------|-------------------| | `BASE_REF` from the operator | External | Checked in T001 | No worktree can be created from the right tree | | `worktree-naming.sh` and its provisioning list | Internal | Checked in T005 | The worktree has no dependencies or build | | `opencode2` with `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | External | Checked in T002 | S8 and every fix brief cannot run | | npm registry or local cache | External | Exercised in T005 | Provisioning fails and the phase stops | | `jq`, `rg` and `shasum` on PATH | Internal | Checked in T002 | The map, verdicts and evidence hashes cannot be built | | `cli-codex` with `gpt-6-luna` | External | Checked in T017 | The review is recorded as skipped and REQ-007 stays open | --- ## 7. ROLLBACK PLAN - **Trigger**: a scenario writes outside the disposable worktree, or the primary checkout gate names a path outside the allowed set. - **Procedure**: keep the worktree until the named paths are read. Write `scratch/worktree/status-before-remove.txt` first. Remove the worktree with `git -C "$RUNROOT" worktree remove "$WT"` and delete its branch with `git -C "$RUNROOT" branch -D "$WT_BRANCH"`. Restore any primary checkout path with `git restore --source="$START" -- `. Delete the new report folder with `rm -r "$REPORT"` only after its contents are copied into this phase folder. Remove the one index row with the edit tool. Record the rollback in `goal.md` section 4. - **Irreversible part**: removing the worktree deletes every uncommitted file in it. The branch deletion makes its commits reachable only through the reflog until git garbage collection. The create command allocates a new number on a rerun, so the same directory name is not reused. --- --- ## L2: PHASE DEPENDENCIES ``` Phase 007 close ──► Setup (T001-T003) ──► Scenario map (T004) │ Worktree + own-code (T005-T007) │ Runner test (T008) ──► Scenarios S1 to S7 (T009) ──► S8 dispatch (T010) │ │ Fix protocol (T011) ◄───────────────┘ │ Results (T012) ──► Report (T013) ──► Index row (T014) │ Primary gate (T015) ──► Worktree removal (T016) ──► Review (T017-T018) ──► Close (T019) ``` | Phase | Depends On | Blocks | |-------|------------|--------| | Setup | Phase 007 close, operator `BASE_REF` | Scenario map, worktree | | Scenario map | Setup | Every run | | Worktree | Setup | Every run | | Runner test | Scenario map, worktree | Scenarios | | Scenarios | Runner test, worktree | Results | | Report | Results | Index row, review | | Removal | Report, primary gate | Close | | Review | Report | Close | --- ## L2: EFFORT ESTIMATION | Phase | Complexity | Estimated Effort | |-------|------------|------------------| | Setup and scenario map | Low | 30 minutes | | Worktree provisioning | Med | 15 to 45 minutes, network bound | | Eight scenario runs | Med | 2 to 4 hours | | Fix attempts | Med | 0 to 2 hours, only on failure | | Report and index row | Low | 1 hour | | Review and close | Low | 30 minutes | | **Total** | | **4 to 8 hours, an assumption with no timed earlier run** | --- ## L2: ENHANCED ROLLBACK ### Pre-deployment Checklist - [ ] `BASE_REF` and `START` recorded in `goal.md` section 4 before the worktree is created - [ ] `git -C "$RUNROOT" status --porcelain` saved to `scratch/status-start.txt` - [ ] No feature flag applies, this phase ships a report and no runtime behavior ### Rollback Procedure 1. Copy every run file and every outcome file into `scratch/report-backup/` before removing anything. 2. Remove the disposable worktree with `git -C "$RUNROOT" worktree remove "$WT"`. 3. Delete its branch with `git -C "$RUNROOT" branch -D "$WT_BRANCH"`. 4. Restore each primary checkout path the gate named with `git restore --source="$START" -- `. 5. Delete the report folder and remove the index row only after step 1. 6. Run `git -C "$RUNROOT" status --porcelain` and compare it with `scratch/status-start.txt`. 7. Record the rollback in `goal.md` section 4. ### Data Reversal - **Has data migrations?** No - **Reversal procedure**: N/A, nothing is written to a database or a remote --- --- ## L3: DEPENDENCY GRAPH ``` ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ Setup │────►│ Scenario map │────►│ Runner │ └────┬─────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ │ │ ┌──────────────┐ ▼ └──────────►│ Worktree │───────►┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ │ own-code │ │ S1 to S8 │────►│ Report │ └──────────────┘ └────┬─────┘ └────┬─────┘ │ │ ┌────▼─────┐ ┌────▼─────┐ │ Fix loop │ │ Review │ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ ``` ### Dependency Matrix | Component | Depends On | Produces | Blocks | |-----------|------------|----------|--------| | Setup | Phase 007 close, `BASE_REF` | Start state | Map, worktree | | Scenario map | Setup | `scenarios.tsv` | Runner | | Worktree | Setup | Own-code proof | Every run | | Runner | Map, worktree | Captured runs | Results | | Fix loop | A failed run | Fix briefs, reruns | Results | | Report | Results | Report package | Index row, review | | Review | Report | Findings | Phase close | --- ## L3: CRITICAL PATH 1. **Worktree provisioning** - 15 to 45 minutes - CRITICAL 2. **Eight scenario runs** - 2 to 4 hours - CRITICAL 3. **Report and review** - 1.5 hours - CRITICAL **Total Critical Path**: about 4 to 7 hours **Parallel Opportunities**: - The scenario map and the worktree creation do not share a file and can run together. - A fix brief and a different scenario run can overlap, because the fix writes one source file and the other scenario runs in a different part of the tree. The conductor keeps at most two workers alive at once, below the three-lane limit. --- ## L3: MILESTONES | Milestone | Description | Success Criteria | Target | |-----------|-------------|------------------|--------| | M1 | Setup done | T001 to T003 marked `[x]` with evidence | Start of phase | | M2 | Own-code worktree | T005 to T007 show `OWN` and no `FOREIGN` | Before the first run | | M3 | Every scenario recorded | Eight run files and eight verdict rows | Mid phase | | M4 | Report published | Report folder, eight outcomes and one index row | Before removal | | M5 | Phase closeable | Every acceptance criterion `Met` | End of phase | --- ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4. ### Roles - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It creates the worktree, runs every scenario, writes every verdict and edits only this phase folder plus the report folder. - **S8 worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. It authors one Level 1 packet inside the disposable worktree, then stops. - **Fix worker**: one dispatch per failed attempt. It may edit exactly one file inside the disposable worktree. - **Reviewer**: one read-only `cli-codex` dispatch at phase close. It writes nothing. ### Pre-Task Checklist - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md` and its `references/worktree-workflows.md` before creating the worktree - [ ] Confirm the conductor's working directory is `RUNROOT`, never the disposable worktree for durable writes - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` - [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/.txt` before dispatching it ### Execution Rules | Rule | Requirement | |------|-------------| | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. T011 runs only after a `FAIL`, and T018 only after a finding | | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief | | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` | | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number | | TASK-SCENARIO | Run the scenario's own command block. Never retype a command from prose | | TASK-HOST | A scenario runs only inside `$WT`. A run started in `$RUNROOT` or `$MAIN` is killed and recorded as a violation | | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` | | TASK-REMOVE | Only the conductor runs the removal block in T016, and only after its status gate prints `REMOVAL_OK` | ### Worker Brief Skeleton Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in: ```text GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION. You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt. Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is: specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/008-playbook-run-in-worktree Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything. A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three failures on the same file. Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run. ROLE: You are a documentation author working in a disposable worktree. You write only the paths named below and you run the verification command before you return. ALLOWED WRITE PATHS: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset, git stash, rm, mv, create.sh outside the task's stated command, generate-context.js, /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS. ``` The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception. ### Dispatch Command ```bash cd "$WT" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \ -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \ "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 & PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null ``` `PHASE` is this folder's path in `RUNROOT`. `WT` is the disposable worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID. ### S8 Brief Task Text Append this text after the skeleton for S8, with the scenario file's Prompt block copied verbatim into the prompt slot: ```text TASK: Author one Level 1 spec packet from the authoring card, following the scenario prompt below exactly. Steps: 1. Read .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md once. 2. Run: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh --skip-branch --level 1 --track zz-playbook-s8 --short-name card-authoring-smoke "Author a Level 1 packet from the card" 3. Fill the four documents it created. Leave implementation-summary.md as created. 4. Run: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh specs/zz-playbook-s8/001-card-authoring-smoke --strict 5. Fix what it reports and run it again, at most three times in all. RETURN exactly one line: the folder path, then the last RESULT line validate.sh printed. ``` ### Status Reporting Format `[T###] DONE | BLOCKED | ESCALATED - one line of evidence`, written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4. ### Blocked Task Protocol 1. Copy the current run files into `scratch/report-backup/` before changing any state. 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output. 3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task. 4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4. --- ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD ### ADR-001: Run the scenario file's own command block **Status**: Accepted **Context**: A runner that retypes commands drifts from the scenario the first time either side changes, and the report then describes the runner rather than the playbook. **Decision**: The runner extracts the first fenced `bash` block under `### Commands` and executes it unchanged. A scenario with no such block is a scenario defect and is escalated. **Consequences**: - The report measures the shipped scenario text. - A scenario that is not copy-runnable fails the phase instead of being silently repaired by the conductor. **Alternatives Rejected**: - Retyping each command from the prose: it hides a defective scenario and adds a second source of truth. ### ADR-002: A disposable worktree with its own dependencies and build **Status**: Accepted **Context**: A fresh worktree has no `node_modules` and no `dist`. Linking either one from the primary checkout makes the run read the primary checkout's code, and the validator can pass without touching the worktree's files. **Decision**: The worktree is created through `worktree-naming.sh create`, which installs every dependency tree and builds the outputs its provisioning list names. A realpath check rejects any build path that resolves outside the worktree. **Consequences**: - Every verdict describes the `BASE_REF` tree. - Provisioning costs 15 to 45 minutes and needs npm access. **Alternatives Rejected**: - Symlinking `node_modules` and `dist`: the documented trap that makes a strict run exit 0 while doing no work. ### ADR-003: Copy the real report file set and keep the ten section headings **Status**: Accepted **Context**: `sk-create-benchmark` section 3 names `benchmark-report.md`, while every existing `system-spec-kit` report folder holds `README.md`, `results.csv`, `source.md` and `outcomes/`. Section 5 requires ten numbered sections. **Decision**: The package copies the observed file set and puts the ten required section headings inside `README.md`. `results.csv` keeps the observed header. **Consequences**: - The new report opens like every sibling report. - A reader who looks for `benchmark-report.md` finds `README.md` instead, and the file table names it. **Alternatives Rejected**: - Adding `benchmark-report.md` beside `README.md`: two report bodies with one verdict each would drift. ### ADR-004: A verdict is a pattern match, and a disagreement is a scenario defect **Status**: Accepted **Context**: A weak executor asked to grade output will call a partial match a pass. **Decision**: Both frozen patterns must match the captured output. When they do not, the conductor reads the scenario's own Pass section. A run that satisfies that section but not the frozen pattern is recorded as `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and escalated to phase 007. **Consequences**: - The same run file yields the same verdict for a second conductor. - A scenario whose wording differs from the frozen pattern costs one escalation instead of a false pass. **Alternatives Rejected**: - A model's judgment of the output: one model is one opinion, and the runs already hold the evidence. ---

{"content":"--- title: "Implementation Plan: Phase 8: playbook-run-in-worktree" description: "Create one disposable sk-git worktree from the operator's BASE_REF, provision it with its own dependencies and build, run the eight phase 007 scenarios from their own command blocks, and publish a report package with one verdict per scenario." trigger_phrases: - "playbook run in worktree plan" - "disposable worktree scenario runner" - "manual testing playbook report package" importance_tier: "normal" contextType: "general" --- # Implementation Plan: Phase 8: playbook-run-in-worktree --- ## 1. SUMMARY ### Technical Context | Aspect | Value | |--------|-------| | **Language/Stack** | Markdown, Bash, Node, npm, git, ripgrep, jq | | **Framework** | system-spec-kit validator and guards, sk-git worktree allocator | | **Storage** | TSV, JSON and text files under this phase's `scratch/`, plus one report folder | | **Testing** | Each scenario file is its own script, compared to a frozen pattern | ### Overview One conductor creates a disposable worktree from the operator's `BASE_REF`, lets the sk-git allocator install that worktree's own dependency trees and build, and proves the build resolves inside the worktree. The conductor then reads the eight scenario rows from the phase 007 playbook index, extracts each scenario's own command block, runs it from the worktree root, captures the output and compares it to a frozen pattern. A failing scenario gets one fix brief and one rerun, at most three times, then an escalation row. The runs are assembled into the benchmark report package before the worktree is removed. --- ## 2. QUALITY GATES ### Definition of Ready - [ ] The launch preconditions in `../spec.md` section 3 are recorded as met in `../goal.md` section 4 - [ ] `BASE_REF` is recorded in `../goal.md` section 4 and resolves with `git rev-parse --verify` - [ ] Phase 007 is closed: every new scenario file exists and the playbook index lists it - [ ] `tasks.md` T001 to T003 are done: preconditions, tools and start state recorded ### Definition of Done - [ ] Every row in `acceptance-criteria.md` is `Met`, `Waived` or `Superseded` - [ ] `bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh --strict` prints `RESULT: PASSED` - [ ] `results.csv` holds eight data rows and every row is `PASS` or an escalated `FAIL` - [ ] The disposable worktree is gone and the primary checkout gate prints nothing outside the allowed paths - [ ] The frontier review ran read-only and its reply is saved --- ## 3. ARCHITECTURE ### Pattern One disposable execution host, one scenario map, one literal runner, one comparator, one report assembler. ### Key Components | Component | Role | |-----------|------| | **Conductor** | One DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session outside OpenCode. It creates the worktree, runs every command, writes every verdict and edits only this phase folder plus the report folder | | **Worktree allocator** | `.skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh create`, which allocates `worktrees/NNN-slug`, creates `.worktrees/NNN-slug` and provisions the dependency trees and builds | | **Scenario map builder** | A Node script that reads the playbook index, selects exactly one row per S label and writes `scratch/scenarios.tsv` | | **Runner** | A Bash script that extracts the `### Commands` fenced block from one scenario file and runs it from the worktree root | | **Comparator** | A Node script that matches each captured run against two frozen patterns and prints `PASS` or `FAIL` with a one-line reason | | **S8 worker** | One `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max` that authors a Level 1 packet from the card inside the disposable worktree | | **Fix worker** | One dispatch per failed attempt, limited to the one file the scenario's source table names | | **Reviewer** | One read-only `cli-codex` dispatch at phase close | ### 3.1 Execution host Two roots are named once by the conductor: - `RUNROOT`: the checkout that holds this phase folder and receives every durable write. It is the build worktree from `../goal.md` section 4 when the operator chose A, otherwise the primary checkout. - `MAIN`: the primary checkout, read with `git -C "$RUNROOT" worktree list --porcelain | awk 'NR==1{print $2}'`. `PHASE` is `$RUNROOT/specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/008-playbook-run-in-worktree`. `WT` is the absolute directory printed by the allocator. `WT_BRANCH` is the branch name printed beside it. `BASE_REF` is the ref the operator recorded in `../goal.md` section 4. The disposable worktree is created from `BASE_REF`, never from the conductor's uncommitted tree: ```bash bash .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh create playbook-run "$BASE_REF" \ > "$PHASE/scratch/worktree/create.out" 2> "$PHASE/scratch/worktree/create.err" read -r WT_BRANCH WT_DIR < "$PHASE/scratch/worktree/create.out" ``` The allocator prints ` ` on stdout and its provisioning lines on stderr. It exits 3 when the worktree exists but provisioning failed. In that case the conductor runs `bash .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh provision "$WT_DIR"` once. A second failure stops the phase with `BLOCKED provisioning`. ### 3.2 Own-code proof A fresh worktree holds no `node_modules` and no `dist`. A wholesale link of either would make the run read the primary checkout's code. The allocator installs each package inside the worktree instead. The conductor proves the result with this Node block, run from `$RUNROOT`, and writes its output to `scratch/worktree/own-code.txt`: ```bash node -e ' const fs = require("fs"); const path = require("path"); const skill = process.argv[1]; const root = fs.realpathSync(process.argv[2]) + path.sep; for (const t of ["runtime/dist", "node_modules", "node_modules/@spec-kit/runtime", "node_modules/@spec-kit/cli", "node_modules/@spec-kit/shared", "runtime/node_modules"]) { const p = path.join(skill, t); if (!fs.existsSync(p)) { console.log("MISSING " + t); continue; } const real = fs.realpathSync(p); console.log((real.startsWith(root) ? "OWN " : "FOREIGN ") + t); }' "$WT/.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit" "$WT" ``` A `FOREIGN` line is a hard stop. A `MISSING runtime/node_modules` line is allowed, as phase 003 records. The built orchestrator is `$WT/.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/dist/lib/validation/orchestrator.js`. ### 3.3 Scenario map (frozen selection rule) Phase 007 owns the scenario ids and file paths. This phase never guesses them. The map builder reads the playbook index and selects one row per S label with the title patterns below. The table also freezes the two pass patterns the comparator uses. | S | Subject | Index title pattern | Pass pattern A | Pass pattern B | |---|---------|---------------------|----------------|----------------| | S1 | Placeholder gate warns in Draft and strict passes | `placeholder.*Draft\|Draft.*placeholder` | `unfilled value token\(s\) in a Draft packet` | `RESULT: PASSED` | | S2 | Placeholder gate errors at Complete | `placeholder.*Complete\|placeholder.*error\|Complete.*placeholder` | `placeholder\(s\) found` | `RESULT: FAILED` | | S3 | A v2.2 doc keeps its old verdict | `placeholder.*v2\.2\|v2\.2.*placeholder\|legacy.*placeholder\|placeholder.*unchanged` | `placeholder\(s\) found` | `RESULT: FAILED` | | S4 | Example drift guard catches a leaked description | `example.*drift\|drift.*example` | `EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK` | empty | | S5 | Golden render holds for every level | `golden` | `Tests\s+12 passed \(12\)` | empty | | S6 | The router loads the card for four intents | `(router\|routing\|intent).*card\|card.*(router\|routing\|intent)` | `^4$` | `^0$` | | S7 | Card sync guard passes and fails on a broken copy | `card.*sync\|sync.*card` | `CARD SYNC OK` | empty | | S8 | DeepSeek authors a Level 1 packet from the card | `(DeepSeek\|weak model).*(author\|packet)\|(author\|packet).*(DeepSeek\|weak model)` | `RESULT: PASSED` | empty | A label with zero matches prints `MISSING S`. A label with two or more matches prints `AMBIGUOUS S`. Either one stops the map build. The conductor then records the blocker and stops, because a guessed scenario is worse than no run. The frozen patterns come from the code phases 003 to 005 ship: the warning text in `validatePlaceholders`, the PLACEHOLDER_FILLED message `placeholder(s) found`, the drift guard sentinel `EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK`, the golden test count `12 passed (12)`, the four intent count and the zero guide count, and the sync guard sentinel `CARD SYNC OK`. ### 3.4 Running one scenario The runner extracts the first fenced `bash` block under `### Commands`, writes it to `scratch/runs/.cmd` and runs it from `$WT`: ```bash awk ' /^### Commands[[:space:]]*$/ { section = 1; next } section && /^```bash[[:space:]]*$/ { block = 1; next } block && /^```[[:space:]]*$/ { exit } block { print } ' "$SCENARIO_FILE" > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$ID.cmd" ``` An empty command file is `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and is not run. The run output goes to `$PHASE/scratch/runs/$ID.txt`, followed by an `exit=` line. The command block is the scenario's own text. The runner never retypes a command. S8 is the one exception. Its commands dispatch a worker, so the conductor extracts the `### Prompt` block, writes a worker brief from the skeleton in this plan, dispatches it inside `$WT`, and then checks the packet the worker returns. S8's packet path is frozen to `specs/zz-playbook-s8/001-card-authoring-smoke` so the check needs no parsing judgment. ### 3.5 Comparator For each run the comparator reads the two patterns and prints one line: `S PASS ` or `S FAIL ` Both patterns must match. The `^4$` and `^0$` patterns are matched with the multiline flag. When a run does not match, the conductor reads the scenario's own `### Pass / Fail` section. If that section states a different observable and the run satisfies it, the row is `SCENARIO_DEFECT` and is escalated to phase 007. The comparator's verdict is never overridden by a chat impression. ### 3.6 Report package An existing report folder holds `README.md`, `results.csv`, `source.md` and `outcomes/`. This phase copies that real file set. The `sk-create-benchmark` report contract requires ten numbered sections, so `README.md` carries all ten section headings even though the older folders use a shorter shape. That difference is recorded in ADR-003. The report folder name is `--manual-testing-playbook--weak-model-authoring`, where the date is the run date from `date +%F`. When the folder exists, the conductor appends `-2`, `-3` and so on, because a report folder is immutable. `results.csv` uses the header observed in the existing folders: ```text scenario_id,runtime,run,evidence_class,verdict ``` One data row per scenario, with `runtime` set to `conductor`, `run` set to `1`, `evidence_class` set to `manual-testing-playbook` and `verdict` set to the row's verdict. `outcomes/.json` follows the observed shape: ```json { "scenarioId": "", "runtime": "conductor", "evidenceClass": "manual-testing-playbook", "verdict": "PASS", "reason": "", "executionContext": { "evidenceRoot": ".", "requireDurableEvidence": true }, "supersedes": [], "providerModel": null, "dispatchModel": "llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max", "runs": [ { "run": "1", "verdict": "PASS", "reason": "", "operatorInputs": "None.", "evidence": [ { "path": "specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/008-playbook-run-in-worktree/scratch/runs/.txt", "bytes": 0, "sha256": "" } ] } ], "evidence": [ { "path": "specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/008-playbook-run-in-worktree/scratch/runs/.txt", "bytes": 0, "sha256": "" } ] } ``` The `bytes` and `sha256` values are filled from `wc -c` and `shasum -a 256`. The example above is a shape, not a literal file. The conductor writes each file from the template in `tasks.md` T013. `source.md` names the scenario files, the run files, the worktree branch and path, `BASE_REF` and the phase folder. `README.md` ends with a file table and a REPRODUCIBILITY section that holds the create, provision and run commands. One row is added at the top of `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/README.md`: ```text | | [`/`](.//) | conductor manual-testing-playbook |

PASS, FAIL | **** | `manual-testing-playbook` | ``` ### 3.7 Failure protocol A `FAIL` row gets one fix brief and one rerun. The same scenario gets at most three fix briefs. After the third failed fix the row becomes `ESCALATED` and the other scenarios continue. The one file a fix may touch is the first row of the scenario file's `## 4. SOURCE FILES` table under `### Implementation And Test Anchors`. The conductor copies that path into the brief and into ALLOWED WRITE PATHS. No second file is allowed. The fix brief is the skeleton in the AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL section, followed by this text with the four fields filled: ```text TASK: Scenario failed at . The captured run is . The failing line is: The scenario's pass criterion is: Change only the single file named under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS so that the scenario passes. Do not edit the scenario file. Do not edit any other file. Run this command from the worktree root and paste its last line: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh --strict RETURN exactly one line: FIXED or BLOCKED ``` After the worker returns, the conductor reruns the same scenario command block from `$WT`. A PASS marks the row `FIXED` and keeps the original run beside the rerun as `scratch/runs/.fix-.txt`. ### Data Flow `BASE_REF`, then disposable worktree, then provable own-code build, then scenario map, then one captured run per scenario, then comparator verdict, then `results.tsv`, then report package, then worktree removal, then frontier review. --- ## FIX ADDENDUM: AFFECTED SURFACES This phase changes no product producer by hand. It reads the phase 007 scenarios and runs the phase 003 to 005 guards. A fix brief may change one file inside the disposable worktree, and that change is never merged by this phase. | Surface | Current Role | Action | Verification | |---------|--------------|--------|--------------| | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/manual-testing-playbook/` | Holds the eight new scenarios and the index | unchanged, read | `scratch/scenarios.tsv` names eight existing files | | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/check-example-drift.sh` | Example drift guard | unchanged, run by S4 | `EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK` in the S4 run | | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/check-card-sync.sh` | Card sync guard | unchanged, run by S7 | `CARD SYNC OK` in the S7 run | | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh` | Validation front end | unchanged, run by S1, S2, S3 and S8 | `RESULT:` line in each run | | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/benchmark/reports/README.md` | Report index | one row added | `rg -c` of the folder name prints `1` | Required inventories: - Same-class producers: the eight scenario files are the whole new set, selected by the eight S labels in `scratch/scenarios.tsv`. A missing label stops the run. - Consumers of changed symbols: the report index is the only consumer changed, and `rg -c` proves one row. - Matrix axes: eight scenarios by two pass patterns, 16 cells, each reported as a match or a miss. - Algorithm invariant: a scenario passes only when its captured run matches both frozen patterns. A disagreement with the scenario file is a scenario defect, never a silent pass. --- ## 4. IMPLEMENTATION PHASES Follow the ordered tasks in `tasks.md`. It owns the Setup, Implementation and Verification phase checkboxes and task state. --- ## 5. TESTING STRATEGY | Test Type | Scope | Tools | |-----------|-------|-------| | Unit | The extractor and comparator against a fixture scenario in `scratch/test/` | `run-scenario.sh`, `check-run.mjs` | | Integration | Each of the eight scenarios, on the disposable worktree | the scenario's own command block | | Manual | The frontier review reads every run and every verdict | read-only `cli-codex` dispatch in `tasks.md` T017 | --- ## 6. DEPENDENCIES | Dependency | Type | Status | Impact if Blocked | |------------|------|--------|-------------------| | `BASE_REF` from the operator | External | Checked in T001 | No worktree can be created from the right tree | | `worktree-naming.sh` and its provisioning list | Internal | Checked in T005 | The worktree has no dependencies or build | | `opencode2` with `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | External | Checked in T002 | S8 and every fix brief cannot run | | npm registry or local cache | External | Exercised in T005 | Provisioning fails and the phase stops | | `jq`, `rg` and `shasum` on PATH | Internal | Checked in T002 | The map, verdicts and evidence hashes cannot be built | | `cli-codex` with `gpt-6-luna` | External | Checked in T017 | The review is recorded as skipped and REQ-007 stays open | --- ## 7. ROLLBACK PLAN - **Trigger**: a scenario writes outside the disposable worktree, or the primary checkout gate names a path outside the allowed set. - **Procedure**: keep the worktree until the named paths are read. Write `scratch/worktree/status-before-remove.txt` first. Remove the worktree with `git -C "$RUNROOT" worktree remove "$WT"` and delete its branch with `git -C "$RUNROOT" branch -D "$WT_BRANCH"`. Restore any primary checkout path with `git restore --source="$START" -- `. Delete the new report folder with `rm -r "$REPORT"` only after its contents are copied into this phase folder. Remove the one index row with the edit tool. Record the rollback in `goal.md` section 4. - **Irreversible part**: removing the worktree deletes every uncommitted file in it. The branch deletion makes its commits reachable only through the reflog until git garbage collection. The create command allocates a new number on a rerun, so the same directory name is not reused. --- --- ## L2: PHASE DEPENDENCIES ``` Phase 007 close ──► Setup (T001-T003) ──► Scenario map (T004) │ Worktree + own-code (T005-T007) │ Runner test (T008) ──► Scenarios S1 to S7 (T009) ──► S8 dispatch (T010) │ │ Fix protocol (T011) ◄───────────────┘ │ Results (T012) ──► Report (T013) ──► Index row (T014) │ Primary gate (T015) ──► Worktree removal (T016) ──► Review (T017-T018) ──► Close (T019) ``` | Phase | Depends On | Blocks | |-------|------------|--------| | Setup | Phase 007 close, operator `BASE_REF` | Scenario map, worktree | | Scenario map | Setup | Every run | | Worktree | Setup | Every run | | Runner test | Scenario map, worktree | Scenarios | | Scenarios | Runner test, worktree | Results | | Report | Results | Index row, review | | Removal | Report, primary gate | Close | | Review | Report | Close | --- ## L2: EFFORT ESTIMATION | Phase | Complexity | Estimated Effort | |-------|------------|------------------| | Setup and scenario map | Low | 30 minutes | | Worktree provisioning | Med | 15 to 45 minutes, network bound | | Eight scenario runs | Med | 2 to 4 hours | | Fix attempts | Med | 0 to 2 hours, only on failure | | Report and index row | Low | 1 hour | | Review and close | Low | 30 minutes | | **Total** | | **4 to 8 hours, an assumption with no timed earlier run** | --- ## L2: ENHANCED ROLLBACK ### Pre-deployment Checklist - [ ] `BASE_REF` and `START` recorded in `goal.md` section 4 before the worktree is created - [ ] `git -C "$RUNROOT" status --porcelain` saved to `scratch/status-start.txt` - [ ] No feature flag applies, this phase ships a report and no runtime behavior ### Rollback Procedure 1. Copy every run file and every outcome file into `scratch/report-backup/` before removing anything. 2. Remove the disposable worktree with `git -C "$RUNROOT" worktree remove "$WT"`. 3. Delete its branch with `git -C "$RUNROOT" branch -D "$WT_BRANCH"`. 4. Restore each primary checkout path the gate named with `git restore --source="$START" -- `. 5. Delete the report folder and remove the index row only after step 1. 6. Run `git -C "$RUNROOT" status --porcelain` and compare it with `scratch/status-start.txt`. 7. Record the rollback in `goal.md` section 4. ### Data Reversal - **Has data migrations?** No - **Reversal procedure**: N/A, nothing is written to a database or a remote --- --- ## L3: DEPENDENCY GRAPH ``` ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ Setup │────►│ Scenario map │────►│ Runner │ └────┬─────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ │ │ ┌──────────────┐ ▼ └──────────►│ Worktree │───────►┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ │ own-code │ │ S1 to S8 │────►│ Report │ └──────────────┘ └────┬─────┘ └────┬─────┘ │ │ ┌────▼─────┐ ┌────▼─────┐ │ Fix loop │ │ Review │ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ ``` ### Dependency Matrix | Component | Depends On | Produces | Blocks | |-----------|------------|----------|--------| | Setup | Phase 007 close, `BASE_REF` | Start state | Map, worktree | | Scenario map | Setup | `scenarios.tsv` | Runner | | Worktree | Setup | Own-code proof | Every run | | Runner | Map, worktree | Captured runs | Results | | Fix loop | A failed run | Fix briefs, reruns | Results | | Report | Results | Report package | Index row, review | | Review | Report | Findings | Phase close | --- ## L3: CRITICAL PATH 1. **Worktree provisioning** - 15 to 45 minutes - CRITICAL 2. **Eight scenario runs** - 2 to 4 hours - CRITICAL 3. **Report and review** - 1.5 hours - CRITICAL **Total Critical Path**: about 4 to 7 hours **Parallel Opportunities**: - The scenario map and the worktree creation do not share a file and can run together. - A fix brief and a different scenario run can overlap, because the fix writes one source file and the other scenario runs in a different part of the tree. The conductor keeps at most two workers alive at once, below the three-lane limit. --- ## L3: MILESTONES | Milestone | Description | Success Criteria | Target | |-----------|-------------|------------------|--------| | M1 | Setup done | T001 to T003 marked `[x]` with evidence | Start of phase | | M2 | Own-code worktree | T005 to T007 show `OWN` and no `FOREIGN` | Before the first run | | M3 | Every scenario recorded | Eight run files and eight verdict rows | Mid phase | | M4 | Report published | Report folder, eight outcomes and one index row | Before removal | | M5 | Phase closeable | Every acceptance criterion `Met` | End of phase | --- ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4. ### Roles - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It creates the worktree, runs every scenario, writes every verdict and edits only this phase folder plus the report folder. - **S8 worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. It authors one Level 1 packet inside the disposable worktree, then stops. - **Fix worker**: one dispatch per failed attempt. It may edit exactly one file inside the disposable worktree. - **Reviewer**: one read-only `cli-codex` dispatch at phase close. It writes nothing. ### Pre-Task Checklist - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md` and its `references/worktree-workflows.md` before creating the worktree - [ ] Confirm the conductor's working directory is `RUNROOT`, never the disposable worktree for durable writes - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` - [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/.txt` before dispatching it ### Execution Rules | Rule | Requirement | |------|-------------| | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. T011 runs only after a `FAIL`, and T018 only after a finding | | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief | | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` | | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number | | TASK-SCENARIO | Run the scenario's own command block. Never retype a command from prose | | TASK-HOST | A scenario runs only inside `$WT`. A run started in `$RUNROOT` or `$MAIN` is killed and recorded as a violation | | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` | | TASK-REMOVE | Only the conductor runs the removal block in T016, and only after its status gate prints `REMOVAL_OK` | ### Worker Brief Skeleton Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in: ```text GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION. You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. ```bash
cd "$RUNROOT"
cat > "$PHASE/scratch/tools/build-scenario-map.cjs" <<'JS'
// Maps the eight frozen scenario labels to the phase 007 playbook rows. The
// title patterns are the only selector, so a renamed row stops the run instead
// of silently mapping the wrong scenario.
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const [indexPath, playbookRoot, outPath] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!indexPath || !playbookRoot || !outPath) {
  console.error('usage: build-scenario-map.cjs <index> <playbook-root> <out.tsv>');
  process.exit(2);
}

const rows = fs.readFileSync(indexPath, 'utf8').split('\n').map((line) => {
  const m = line.match(/^\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)]+)\)\s*\|/);
  return m ? { id: m[1].trim(), title: m[2].trim(), file: m[3].trim() } : null;
}).filter(Boolean);

const labels = [
  ['S1', /placeholder.*draft|draft.*placeholder/i, 'unfilled value token\\(s\\) in a Draft packet', 'RESULT: PASSED'],
  ['S2', /placeholder.*complete|placeholder.*error|complete.*placeholder/i, 'placeholder\\(s\\) found', 'RESULT: FAILED'],
  ['S3', /placeholder.*v2\\.2|v2\\.2.*placeholder|legacy.*placeholder|placeholder.*unchanged/i, 'placeholder\\(s\\) found', 'RESULT: FAILED'],
  ['S4', /example.*drift|drift.*example/i, 'EXAMPLE_DRIFT_OK', ''],
  ['S5', /golden/i, 'Tests\\s+12 passed \\(12\\)', ''],
  ['S6', /(router|routing|intent).*card|card.*(router|routing|intent)/i, '^4$', '^0$'],
  ['S7', /card.*sync|sync.*card/i, 'CARD SYNC OK', ''],
  ['S8', /(deepseek|weak model).*(author|packet)|(author|packet).*(deepseek|weak model)/i, 'RESULT: PASSED', ''],
];

const out = [];
const problems = [];
for (const [label, re, passA, passB] of labels) {
  const hits = rows.filter((row) => re.test(row.title));
  if (hits.length !== 1) {
    problems.push(`${hits.length === 0 ? 'MISSING' : 'AMBIGUOUS'} ${label}`);
    continue;
  }
  const hit = hits[0];
  const abs = path.resolve(playbookRoot, hit.file);
  if (!fs.existsSync(abs)) {
    problems.push(`NO_FILE ${label} ${hit.file}`);
    continue;
  }
  out.push([label, hit.id, abs, passA, passB].join('\t'));
}

if (problems.length > 0) {
  console.log(problems.join('\n'));
  process.exit(1);
}
fs.writeFileSync(outPath, out.join('\n') + '\n');
console.log(`SCENARIO_MAP_OK ${out.length}`);
JS

  "$RUNROOT/$S/manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md" \
  "$RUNROOT/$S/manual-testing-playbook" \
  "$PHASE/scratch/scenarios.tsv"

**Objective:** Run every new or changed manual-testing-playbook scenario from phase 007 inside one disposable sk-git worktree and publish a captured, scripted PASS or FAIL for each one.

### Decisions

Frozen choices. Changing one is an amendment.

| ID | Decision |
|----|----------|
| D1 | The only scenario host is one disposable worktree created through `worktree-naming.sh create` from the operator's `BASE_REF`. The primary checkout never runs a scenario. |
| D2 | Every scenario runs from its own `### Commands` fenced block. The conductor never retypes a command. |
| D3 | A verdict is a match against two frozen patterns in `scratch/scenarios.tsv`. A run that satisfies the scenario's own Pass section but not the pattern is a `SCENARIO_DEFECT`, not a pass. |
| D4 | A failed scenario gets one fix brief and one rerun, at most three times. After the third failed fix the row becomes `ESCALATED` and the other scenarios continue. |
| D5 | The report package copies the real file set of an existing report folder: `README.md`, `results.csv`, `source.md` and `outcomes/`. The ten `sk-create-benchmark` section headings live inside `README.md`. |
| D6 | Durable writes land in this phase folder plus the one report folder and one reports index row. No source file under `.skilled/` is edited by hand. |
| D7 | The report folder is written before the worktree is removed, so no evidence depends on a deleted directory. |

<!-- ANCHOR:what-built -->
## What Was Built

Nothing is built yet. This summary is rewritten when the phase closes.

### Phase 8: playbook-run-in-worktree

When it runs, this phase creates one disposable worktree from the operator's `BASE_REF`, proves the worktree builds and runs its own code, executes the eight scenarios phase 007 added, and writes a report package with one outcome file per scenario. The report lets phase 009 and the operator see which new behaviors were proved and which were escalated without opening a chat transcript.

### Files Changed

| File | Action | Purpose |
|------|--------|---------|
| `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md`, `goal.md` | Created | Phase plan, written before execution |
| `scratch/scenarios.tsv`, `scratch/results.tsv`, `scratch/verdicts.md` | Planned | Scenario map, verdict rows and the verdict page |
| `<report folder>/README.md`, `results.csv`, `source.md`, `outcomes/*.json` | Planned | The report package |
<!-- /ANCHOR:what-built -->

---

<!-- ANCHOR:how-delivered -->
## How It Was Delivered

Not delivered yet. The phase runs as a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash conductor under the protocol in `plan.md`, section AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL. One disposable worktree hosts every scenario, and one read-only frontier review closes the phase.
<!-- /ANCHOR:how-delivered -->

---

<!-- ANCHOR:decisions -->
## Key Decisions

| Decision | Why |
|----------|-----|
| Run each scenario's own command block | A retyped command would test the conductor's copy rather than the playbook |
| Provision the worktree with its own dependencies and build | A symlinked `node_modules` or `dist` would make the run read the primary checkout's code |
| Copy the real report file set and keep the ten required sections | The new report opens like its siblings and still meets the benchmark report contract |
| A mismatch with the scenario Pass section is a scenario defect | The conductor must not grade a scenario it is not allowed to edit |
<!-- /ANCHOR:decisions -->

---

<!-- ANCHOR:verification -->
## Verification

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Strict validation of this phase folder | Run at phase close by `tasks.md` T019 |
| Eight scenario verdicts | Run and recorded by `tasks.md` T009 to T012 |
| Primary checkout gate | Run by `tasks.md` T015 |
| Report package shape | Run by `tasks.md` T013 |
<!-- /ANCHOR:verification -->

---

<!-- ANCHOR:limitations -->
## Known Limitations

1. **One run per scenario.** A pass is one sample on one `BASE_REF`, not a stability claim.
2. **S8 samples one model.** The authoring run uses DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max only.
3. **Provisioning needs npm access.** A machine with no registry or cache cannot run this phase.
<!-- /ANCHOR:limitations -->
